Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: A line of vehicles waits at a traffic light. It has at least one truck ten meters long, and at least one car four meters long. There is a two meter gap between neighboring vehicles, and no gap at either end of the line. Which total length of the line is impossible?

They ask what's impossible. So every length we can really build is out, and we cross out three choices. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, by plugging in the answers, and then with an insight about the gaps.

[short pause] Let's start by plugging in the answers, and build lines in order. The question says at least one of each, so we have no choice. The shortest line has one truck and one car, with one gap between them.
Ten for the truck, plus two for the gap, is twelve. Twelve plus four for the car is sixteen meters. Sixteen is choice number one. We just built it, so it's possible, and choice number one is out.
at: and choice number one is out

slides.say: Now a tip for quick adding. Every extra vehicle comes with its own gap, so let's glue each vehicle to its gap. A car plus a gap is four plus two, six. A truck plus a gap is ten plus two, twelve.
Let's add one more car to our sixteen. Sixteen plus six is twenty-two. That's choice number three, so it's possible, and it's out.
Choice number four is twenty-eight. Let's add another car. Twenty-two plus six is twenty-eight. Possible, so it's out too.

Only choice number two is left, twenty. Let's see why it can't be built. Sixteen is the shortest line. The smallest thing we can add is a car with its gap, six meters. That jumps from sixteen straight to twenty-two, and skips right over twenty. So twenty is impossible, and choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the insight. Let's give every vehicle the gap that comes after it. Then each truck counts as ten plus two, twelve, and each car as four plus two, six. But the last vehicle has no gap after it, because there's no gap at the end. So we take two away, once.
So the length plus two is made of twelves and sixes only. Twelve and six both divide by six. So the length plus two always divides by six.

Now we check that condition on the choices. Sixteen plus two is eighteen, and eighteen divides by six. Twenty plus two is twenty-two, and twenty-two doesn't divide by six. So twenty can never be the length. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: twenty can never be the length
